stem: If $X=\{ {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3} \}$, $Y=\{ {=b1}, {=b2}, {=b3}, {=e} \}$, and R is a relation from X to Y where a R b means: «b = a + {=k}», for each $a\in X$, $b\in Y$. Write R as a set of ordered pairs, listing the pairs in order of a, as (a, b), (a, b), …
solution: When a = {=x1}: b = {=x1} + {=k} = {=b1}, so the pair is ({=x1}, {=b1}).
When a = {=x2}: b = {=x2} + {=k} = {=b2}, so the pair is ({=x2}, {=b2}).
When a = {=x3}: b = {=x3} + {=k} = {=b3}, so the pair is ({=x3}, {=b3}).
notes: Basic entry: one-step rule, every image lies in Y (Y has one extra element 'e' that is never an image). Answer is the list of pairs in increasing a.
